rationale: Inbox intake of the founder's own Substack essay (34 pp., text generated by Kimi and Fable). The item does not carry the 'THIS DOCUMENT IS THE LEDGER'S SOURCE' marker and the report's stated footing is discovery material, so the essay is supplier's words: it is already in the ledger as SRC-JHONG-2026 and no claims or evidence are catalogued from it here. Of the 29 works the essay names, 25 resolved to nothing on OpenAlex; four resolved to DOI candidates, but none yielded text (two landing pages returned only the word 'Redirecting', two returned HTTP 403), and in all four cases the candidate's OpenAlex title indicates a different work from the one the essay meant (a 2019 fibromyalgia diagnostic-criteria paper rather than 1990s community tender-point surveys; a review of regression cases spanning 1900–1987 rather than Everson & Cole's classic; an arthroscopy-for-osteoarthritis trial whose title does not describe a sham-surgery design; a 2022 PIEZO review rather than the discovery paper or the prize). Each wrong candidate is dispositioned failed and the work meant stays blocked or irrelevant. Ten named works are duplicates of records the ledger already holds; three (Stecco densification, Moseley cortical smudging, the Johnson X thread) remain blocked pending primary text; the rest concern the essay's euphoria, cascade-warning and repair-ceiling sections, which carry no ledger claim. No URL was reached for any text, so no url correction is owed. No new evidence, claims, or sources enter; the edition is unchanged, which after a pass that verified nothing new is the correct outcome. VASO-R010 already covers the one retrieval route worth pressing (the tender-point-count surveys), so no new research item is added.
